verdict: Gusto: Choose Gusto when US SMB payroll and benefits with transparent published pricing is the job — not when you need a full HRIS, people platform, or dedicated ATS. Scores use the HR editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing.
weaknesses: Many expected HR features are add-ons
AI is not a product pillar
bestFor: US small businesses running payroll (and benefits) for the first time
Teams that want published month-to-month pricing instead of HCM quotes
Single-state companies that can start on Simple and upgrade for multi-state
notIdealFor: Companies whose primary job is a full HRIS or people platform
High-volume recruiting / structured hiring ATS buyers
Global EOR or 1,000+ employee HCM buyers
tradeoffs: Published free tiers vs paid depth for ATS, WFM, time, or training jobs
Hub / multi-module pricing complexity vs single-product floors
Mobile/frontline readiness vs desk-bound admin depth
Opaque contact-sales pricing vs transparent published seats
recommendation: Choose Gusto when US SMB payroll and benefits with transparent published pricing is the job — not when you need a full HRIS, people platform, or dedicated ATS. Compare Rippling for HR+IT+payroll unification, BambooHR for a stronger core HRIS, Justworks for PEO, and Deel for global hiring.
editorialNotes: HR Priority-1 batch. Approved on hr-editorial v1.0.0. membershipRole=primary. jobCluster=payroll-benefits. handsOnTesting=false. Affiliate economics excluded.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Gusto’s payroll UX is the SMB default for non-experts with transparent published prices. Score is research-grounded, not lab-tested.
Primary job is payroll-benefits. Scored inside that cluster — strong payroll/benefits fit, not an ATS or WFM.
Pay runs, tax filings, and benefits admin are solid for SMB. HRIS/performance/time are thinner or add-on — held at 7.
Accounting and time-clock connectors (QuickBooks, Xero, Homebase-class) are adequate; not a 600-app people platform.
Employee pay stubs and time add-ons exist; not a deskless WFM app.
Payroll reports are table-stakes; people analytics are not the product thesis.
Clear Simple → Plus → Premium path for SMB; mid-market/enterprise payroll (ADP/Paylocity) is a different shortlist.
Transparent $49+$6 floor and month-to-month cancel story are strong; add-ons and multi-state upgrades raise TCO. Affiliate economics excluded.
AI is not a primary marketed payroll pillar on the pricing page — scored low versus Bamboo/Rippling/Greenhouse AI stories.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the nine HR editorial criteria using the category weights (hiring/workforce fit 15, workflow depth 14, ease of use 12, integrations 12, value 12, mobile/frontline 10, scalability 9, analytics 8, AI 8), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — ATS, core HRIS, payroll/benefits, people-platform, frontline WFM, time & attendance, SOP training, and LMS peers are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score, and affiliate economics are excluded.
